Turnover and nestedness of presence/absence dissimilarity

Source: R/beta_partition.r
sorensen_turnover.Rd

Baselga's partition of the Sorensen and Jaccard dissimilarities between two samples into turnover (features replaced by others) and nestedness-resultant dissimilarity (one sample holding a subset of the other's features).

Usage

sorensen_turnover(
  counts,
  margin = 1L,
  pairs = NULL,
  clust = NULL,
  cpus = n_cpus()
)

sorensen_nestedness(
  counts,
  margin = 1L,
  pairs = NULL,
  clust = NULL,
  cpus = n_cpus()
)

jaccard_turnover(
  counts,
  margin = 1L,
  pairs = NULL,
  clust = NULL,
  cpus = n_cpus()
)

jaccard_nestedness(
  counts,
  margin = 1L,
  pairs = NULL,
  clust = NULL,
  cpus = n_cpus()
)

Arguments

counts

A numeric matrix of count data (samples \(\times\) features). Counts are converted to presence/absence. Values must not be negative.

margin

The margin containing samples. 1 if samples are rows, 2 if samples are columns. Ignored when counts is a special object class (e.g. phyloseq). Default: 1

pairs

Which combinations of samples should distances be calculated for? The default value (NULL) calculates all-vs-all. Provide a numeric or logical vector specifying positions in the distance matrix to calculate. See examples.

clust

Whether and how to cluster the samples (rows and columns) before returning the distance matrix: NULL (the default) or FALSE to keep them in their input order, or one of stats::hclust()'s linkage methods, "average" (UPGMA), "complete", "single", "ward.D", "ward.D2", "mcquitty" (WPGMA), "median" or "centroid", or "pcoa" to order them along the first axis of pcoa(). Clustering reorders the samples of the result, with their labels (samples without names are labelled with their positions in the input): its order attribute gives each one's position in the input, so that meta[attr(d, "order"), ] lines metadata up with them. ecodive's ordinations and tests put the samples back in their input order before analysing them, so give them metadata in its usual order. Other packages see the reordered matrix: give them metadata reordered by order, or matched by name. The matrix's display list keeps clust (FALSE as "none"; see ecodive_display), which plot.ecodive_dist() follows: with NULL it clusters the samples for the heatmap ("average"), and with "none" it keeps their order. clust needs every distance, so it cannot be used with pairs. rho_p()'s similarities are clustered as \(1 - \rho_p\).

cpus

How many parallel processing threads should be used. The default, n_cpus(), is the CPU cores this R process may use, within any limits set on it. Results are the same for any cpus.

Value

A distance matrix: a dist object of class c("ecodive_dist", "dist"), as beta_div() returns.

Details

With \(a\) features in both samples, and \(b\) and \(c\) only in the first and only in the second (Baselga 2010, 2012):

FunctionComponentFormula
sorensen()Sorensen dissimilarity (total)\(\frac{b + c}{2a + b + c}\)
sorensen_turnover()Simpson dissimilarity, \(\beta_{sim}\)\(\frac{\min(b, c)}{a + \min(b, c)}\)
sorensen_nestedness()nestedness-resultant, \(\beta_{sne}\)\(\beta_{sor} - \beta_{sim}\)
jaccard()Jaccard dissimilarity (total)\(\frac{b + c}{a + b + c}\)
jaccard_turnover()\(\beta_{jtu}\)\(\frac{2\min(b, c)}{a + 2\min(b, c)}\)
jaccard_nestedness()\(\beta_{jne}\)\(\beta_{jac} - \beta_{jtu}\)

Turnover is 0 when one sample's features are a subset of the other's, and 1 when the samples share none; nestedness is 0 when they have the same number of features. Turnover and nestedness add up to the total, sorensen() or jaccard().

When a sample has no features, turnover and nestedness are undefined (NaN), as in abdiv and betapart, although the total is 1 (or NaN when both samples are empty).

Neither component is a metric: a sample nested in two others has turnover 0 to both, while they can have turnover 1 to each other.

The partition is debated: Podani & Schmera (2011) and Carvalho et al. (2012) split the same totals differently, into replacement and richness difference (adespatial's beta.div.comp()). See Baselga & Leprieur (2015) for a comparison.

Same names in other packages: abdiv's functions are named sorenson_turnover() and sorenson_nestedness() (with an "o"), and jaccard_turnover() and jaccard_nestedness(), taking two vectors; they give the same values. betapart's beta.pair() returns all three matrices of a family, as beta_partition() does.

Input Types

The counts parameter is designed to accept a simple numeric matrix, but seamlessly supports objects from the following biological data packages:

  • phyloseq

  • rbiom

  • SummarizedExperiment

  • TreeSummarizedExperiment

For large datasets, standard matrix operations may be slow. See vignette('performance') for details on using optimized formats (e.g. sparse matrices) and parallel processing.

References

Baselga, A. (2010). Partitioning the turnover and nestedness components of beta diversity. Global Ecology and Biogeography, 19, 134-143. doi:10.1111/j.1466-8238.2009.00490.x

Baselga, A. (2012). The relationship between species replacement, dissimilarity derived from nestedness, and nestedness. Global Ecology and Biogeography, 21, 1223-1232. doi:10.1111/j.1466-8238.2011.00756.x

Lennon, J. J., Koleff, P., Greenwood, J. J. D., & Gaston, K. J. (2001). The geographical structure of British bird distributions: diversity, spatial turnover and scale. Journal of Animal Ecology, 70, 966-979. doi:10.1046/j.0021-8790.2001.00563.x

Podani, J., & Schmera, D. (2011). A new conceptual and methodological framework for exploring and explaining pattern in presence-absence data. Oikos, 120, 1625-1638. doi:10.1111/j.1600-0706.2011.19451.x

Carvalho, J. C., Cardoso, P., & Gomes, P. (2012). Determining the relative roles of species replacement and species richness differences in generating beta-diversity patterns. Global Ecology and Biogeography, 21, 760-771. doi:10.1111/j.1466-8238.2011.00694.x

Baselga, A., & Leprieur, F. (2015). Comparing methods to separate components of beta diversity. Methods in Ecology and Evolution, 6, 1069-1079. doi:10.1111/2041-210X.12388

See also

beta_partition() for the three matrices of a family at once, beta_partition_multi() for whole sets of samples, beta_div().

Other Partitioned metrics: beta_partition(), beta_partition_multi(), bray_balanced()

Examples

    sorensen_turnover(ex_counts)
#> # A dist: 4 samples (lower triangle)
#> # Simpson Dissimilarity (Sorensen Turnover)
#>       Saliva Gums Nose
#> Gums    0
#> Nose    0     0
#> Stool   0.25  0.2    0
#> # Attributes: method
    sorensen_nestedness(ex_counts)
#> # A dist: 4 samples (lower triangle)
#> # Sorensen Nestedness
#>       Saliva      Gums   Nose
#> Gums  0.111
#> Nose  0.2       0.0909
#> Stool 0.0833 -5.55e-17 0.0909
#> # Attributes: method

    # Turnover + nestedness = total.
    all.equal(
      as.vector(jaccard_turnover(ex_counts) + jaccard_nestedness(ex_counts)),
      as.vector(jaccard(ex_counts)) )
#> [1] TRUE
